sights.w: 26 m mound in Tennōji Park long held to be a 5th-century kofun; it was Tokugawa Ieyasu's HQ in the Winter Siege and Sanada Yukimura's in the Summer Siege of Osaka (1614–15). Summit markers explain the battle.
Small hillside shrine on the Tennōji slopes where Sanada Yukimura is said to have fallen in 1615; also linked to Sugawara no Michizane.

sights.n: Sankō Shrine & Sanada Yukimura statue (三光神社)
sights.w: Tamatsukuri shrine guarding a bronze statue of Sanada Yukimura and the 'Sanada tunnel' entrance near the site of his Sanada-maru fort.

Neighbourhood sentō near Dōbutsuen-mae with a ceiling painting of 108 carp, soft water throughout and a 110°C Mt Fuji lava-stone sauna; open from 6am (closed Mon). Featured by Time Out Osaka and All About.
